cases.summary: Copying a cloud use string.replace which can replace more than intended
cases.description:
### Jenkins and plugins versions report

<details>
  <summary>Environment</summary>

  <!-- Paste your environment details below -->
  ```text
Jenkins 2.549
kubernetes plugin
  ```

</details>


### What Operating System are you using (both controller, and any agents involved in the problem)?

not relevant

### Reproduction steps

1. install jclouds plugin
2. create a kubernetes cloud with name `kube`
3. create a template in that cloud that has the same name as the cloud itself, i.e. `kube`
4. on create new cloud with name `kube2` by selecting to copy from an existing cloud and choose the `kube`

### Expected Results

the new copied cloud should have a template with name `kube`

### Actual Results

the new cloud has a template with name `kube2`

### Anything else?

_No response_

### Are you interested in contributing a fix?

caused by #7658 that uses string replace

evidence.eventual_fix_title: Avoid using string replace when copying a cloud
evidence.eventual_fix_problem_statement:
Avoid using string replace when copying a cloud

there is just no need to do a potentially problematic replace when the name field is no longer final.
The `replace` will match more than once, so if there is another occurrence of `<name>cloudname</name>` in the xml that will be replaced as well. Some clouds that define templates also use fields with name `name`. If that name is identical to the cloud name that would change as well.

fixes #26259
